description: Minimal curated representative-media robustness evaluation set for tests/test_matching_robustness.py, exercising the existing M2-02 match_cue baseline (src/audio_cue_locator/infrastructure/acoustic_matching/baseline.py) against docs/matching-contract.md and docs/matching-baseline.md, which this manifest does not redefine. Every asset/cue array is a plain list of finite floats; the consuming test converts each to a CANONICAL_AUDIO_SPEC-conformant (mono, float32) numpy array itself -- this manifest does not declare its own sample rate, since the canonical sample rate is owned by CANONICAL_AUDIO_SPEC and must not be duplicated here (mirroring tests/fixtures/matching/manifest.json's own convention). Unlike M2-03's manifest, which used short arbitrary numeric sequences purely to exercise degenerate-input handling, every signal in this manifest is a deterministic synthetic harmonic construction (440 Hz + 880 Hz components with a Hann envelope) chosen to have non-trivial spectral/temporal shape more representative of an acoustic cue than a short arbitrary sequence, while remaining fully synthetic, reproducible, and free of any external-asset reuse-rights concern. Every case's expected outcome and evidentiary values were verified by directly invoking the existing, unmodified match_cue baseline during authoring (a private computation, not a pytest run); tests/test_matching_robustness.py independently re-invokes match_cue against these same arrays and asserts the documented values.

provenance.reuse_rights_statement: No external representative-media asset (no downloaded, recorded, or third-party audio/video file) is used anywhere in this manifest. Every cue and source array is a deterministic, synthetically generated NumPy float array constructed by a documented formula (harmonic burst with Hann envelope; single continuous tone; additive Gaussian noise from a fixed, documented seed) and embedded directly as plain-list sample data, exactly as tests/fixtures/matching/manifest.json already does for M2-03. No third-party reuse-rights, licensing, or attribution obligation applies to any asset in this manifest.
provenance.existing_m1_era_fixtures_reuse_reason: tests/fixtures/ already holds unrelated M1-era media fixtures (not_media.txt, no_audio_stream.mp4, sine_440hz_mono_1s.wav, video_with_audio.mp4). tests/test_canonicalization_fixtures.py's own module docstring already states these do not represent real-world/representative matching material (they exist to exercise M1's canonicalization/probing error handling, not acoustic cue matching): none of them carry a documented cue occurrence, ground-truth position, or absence label, and reusing them here would require inventing matching semantics for assets designed for a different purpose. They are therefore not reused by this issue's representative evaluation set; this decision resolves state gap G6.
provenance.generation_method: Authored once via a private Python script that imports the existing, unmodified match_cue baseline directly (no repository files were modified by that script) to compute and verify each case's expected_outcome/expected_score/expected_timestamp_seconds/expected_diagnostic_best_score against the real algorithm, rather than by hand-derived analysis alone (feasible for M2-03's short arbitrary arrays, impractical to hand-verify by exact arithmetic for this manifest's 240-sample harmonic and noise-perturbed arrays). This is fixture-authoring tooling, not test execution: tests/test_matching_robustness.py independently re-invokes match_cue at test time and asserts against these same documented values; no pytest run was performed while authoring this manifest.

ffmpeg_probing_status.checked_via: which ffmpeg ffprobe (read-only, no repository/adapter change)
ffmpeg_probing_status.blocking_impact: ffmpeg/ffprobe remain unavailable in this environment (re-confirmed at implementation time, consistent with canonical_audio.py's own PENDING_LIVE_PROBING_VERIFICATION and states/M2/M2-04/issue-operational-state.json gap G2). This blocks (a) decoding any real encoded audio/video asset for use as a representative cue/source in this evaluation, and (b) performing a genuine lossy-compression round-trip perturbation. As a direct consequence, every signal in this manifest is a synthetically constructed, already-canonical-shaped array (mirroring M2-01/M2-02/M2-03's own synthetic-array convention), not a decoded real-media asset; no canonicalization/decode preprocessing step is exercised by this evaluation at all, so 'preprocessing effects' are explicitly not present here, distinct from and never conflated with the matcher (match_cue) effects that this manifest does measure (amplitude/noise robustness of the normalized-correlation algorithm itself).

omitted.reason: Not evaluated in this issue. ffmpeg/ffprobe are unavailable in this implementation environment (re-confirmed via 'which ffmpeg ffprobe' at implementation time; see ffmpeg_probing_status above). Independently of availability, the existing FFmpegMediaAdapter (src/audio_cue_locator/infrastructure/media_processing/ffmpeg_adapter.py) exposes only probe() and extract_audio() (decode-to-WAV extraction); it does not expose a lossy-codec encoding operation, so a genuine compression round-trip perturbation cannot be performed through the project's sole authorized ffmpeg/ffprobe boundary without adding new adapter capability, which is out of scope and a forbidden path for this issue (implementation_handoff.files_guidance.files_out_of_scope). This omission is explicit and documented, not implied by absence, per formal issue section 8 acceptance criterion 2.

cases.description: Representative harmonic-burst cue (440Hz+880Hz, Hann-enveloped, 240 samples) embedded verbatim (scaled by 1.0) at a known offset inside an otherwise silent 1920-sample source. Amplitude perturbation of 1.0 tests robustness to loudness variation; normalized cross-correlation is provably invariant to positive scalar amplitude scaling of an otherwise-unperturbed occurrence (Cauchy-Schwarz equality), so the score is expected to remain 1.0 regardless of scale.
cases.provenance: Synthetically generated in this manifest via a deterministic harmonic+Hann-envelope formula; no external asset, no reuse-rights concern.

cases.description: A continuous 300Hz tone source (no embedded occurrence of the cue) against the same representative harmonic-burst cue. Verifies genuine discrimination (not an artificially zero-sum construction): the cue's spectral/temporal shape (440Hz+880Hz harmonic burst with Hann envelope) does not appear anywhere in a plain continuous 300Hz tone, so no lag should reach the 0.75 acceptance threshold.
cases.provenance: Synthetically generated in this manifest via a deterministic single-tone formula; no external asset, no reuse-rights concern.

cases.description: Representative harmonic-burst cue occurrence embedded at the known offset with additive Gaussian noise (seed=20260904, sigma=0.05) applied only within the occurrence window, approximating measured SNR 18.30 dB. Noise breaks the verbatim-shape invariance so the score is expected to be less than 1.0; the analytically predicted score under the independent-noise approximation 1/sqrt(1 + noise_energy/clean_energy) is 0.992691 (documented for comparison, not asserted as the authoritative value -- the authoritative expected_score is match_cue's own directly computed output).
